transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (CTO, LifeCare), Priya Rao (Head of Security), Ben Carter (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick intro, deep dive on private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency in eu-west-1, egress IP allowlist, BYOK KMS integration, POC success criteria and benchmark plan, timeline for a 2-week POC. Agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this, short agenda — confirm objectives, networking options (peering/private link), regions and egress, success criteria and sizing, then agree a POC timeline.
[00:18] Miguel: yeah thanks, we're keen to scope this POC to validate we can keep PHI in region and not leak to public internet. primary concern is data residency + being able to run inference behind our VPC.
[00:30] Priya: and from security— we need KMS BYOK, audit logs, and an allowlist for egress IPs, also SOC2 docs to review.
[00:42] Samira: got it, thanks. quick call out — we support three deployment paths that are relevant: hosted with PrivateLink, Redwood Dedicated in your VPC via VPC peering/Transit, or full Private (on-prem/VPC Peering with private control plane). each has tradeoffs on latency, operational overhead, and egress profile.
[01:10] Ben: can you explain the differences again? peering vs private link, like from a network perspective?
[01:20] Samira: sure. VPC peering is a direct route between your VPC and our serving VPC — it's good for low-latency, predictable routing, but you need to manage routes and maybe a transit gateway if multiple VPCs. PrivateLink (AWS VPC endpoint) gives you an endpoint in your VPC that routes to our service over the AWS internal network, and it simplifies allowlisting because the endpoint is in your account, but with PrivateLink there's an ENI and there are limits on throughput per endpoint unless you scale endpoints.
[01:58] Miguel: throughput limits — is that a hard blocker? we have spikes when clinicians run batch summarizations overnight, maybe 200 req/s bursts.
[02:10] Samira: it's not a blocker; for bursts we'd either recommend dedicated capacity (reserved pool) or multiple PrivateLink endpoints + load balancing. for Dedicated / private deployments we can provision a GPU pool sized for your 200 qps burst and autoscale for steady state.
[02:34] Jordan: also worth calling out egress: if you're in eu-west-1 and want zero egress to public internet, peering or PrivateLink both can keep traffic on AWS backbone, but you need to ensure your routing/NAT config doesn't SNAT to an internet gateway. Priya, that ties to your allowlist ask — we can provide IP blocks if you need firm IPs.
[02:58] Priya: yes we need static egress IPs for our firewall vendor. do you provide fixed IP ranges for the POC?
[03:06] Samira: for hosted PrivateLink we can give the endpoint DNS and recommend an allowlist, but the IPs are managed by AWS so less stable; for Dedicated peering we can negotiate with infra to announce stable egress IPs from our side or you can route through a NAT with Elastic IPs in your account. we'll put that in the checklist.
[03:36] Ben: region question — we need eu data to stay in eu-west-1, does Redwood support pinning the model and inference in that region?
[03:45] Samira: yes, we can pin serving to eu-west-1 for the POC. model versioning is supported so you can pin to a verified snapshot. note: there may be small differences in latency vs us-west, but region pinning ensures data residency.
[03:58] Miguel: success criteria — we'd like p50 latency under 200ms for single-turn clinical summarization, throughput of 100 sustained and 200 burst, and no logs leaving the region, plus audit logs for every request. will that be feasible?
[04:18] Samira: technically feasible. two clarifications: 1) p50 200ms depends on sequence length and model size — what model and average prompt length do you expect? 2) audit logs — do you mean request/response payloads or only metadata?
[04:36] Miguel: good point. we'll target a 5-10 token summary length on average with 300 token inputs (clinical notes). model few-shot, probably an Llama-2-70B-like open model or equivalent quantized variant. audit logs — metadata only initially (timestamp, request id, user id, model version), not full PII payloads stored.
[05:00] Samira: with 300 tokens in, 10 tokens out, on a quantized 70B variant, p50 200ms is tight but achievable on a dedicated GPU pool with optimized kernels. if you need hosted variants we might see p50 closer to 300-400ms. we'll put recommended configs in the benchmark spec.
[05:25] Jordan: timeline idea — 2 week POC: week 1 network setup (peering/PrivateLink), baseline smoke tests, week 2 run the bench (load + accuracy checks) and final review. does that map to your expectations?
[05:40] Miguel: that's reasonable. need to sync with infra — Ben can confirm CIDR ranges and schedule maintenance windows.
[05:48] Ben: yep i can do that. one other constraint — our infra team requires a security design review before allowing peering. Priya will lead that.
[05:58] Priya: yes i'll need the network diagram and the KMS key policy. do you support BYOK for encryption at rest?
[06:08] Samira: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private deployments and Dedicated; for hosted we offer KMS integration where we can integrate with your KMS via a cross-account role — we will document the exact flow. Key rotation policies we can support, and we emit audit logs to CloudTrail/your SIEM.
[06:30] Miguel: benchmarks — what will you run? lat/throughput only or also quality/regression tests?
[06:38] Samira: both. proposed benchmark plan in the POC: 1) baseline latency/throughput with synthetic traffic (same token distribution as your production sample), 2) end-to-end latency including client->VPC peering->serving->response, 3) quality eval on a 500-1,000 prompt holdout set for clinical summarization metrics (ROUGE/F1 or custom scoring), 4) failure/fallback scenarios (model OOM, degraded capacity, automatic fallback to smaller model). we'll provide a harness and scripts.
[07:10] Jordan: we'll share a benchmark spec doc and a sample dataset link (we'll expect anonymized notes). Ben, you'll run the network prep and provide the CIDRs.
[07:20] Ben: noted. regarding the sample dataset — we can't include PHI in the shared set, so we'll either anonymize or use synthetic data.
[07:28] Samira: synthetic is fine for performance. for quality eval you can provide a de-identified set or run the eval in your VPC and share aggregated metrics. we can support both flows.
[07:40] Miguel: what about costs — Dedicated vs Hosted PrivateLink? highlight differences so we can justify to procurement.
[07:50] Jordan: in short, Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) is higher fixed cost but gives you predictable latency, can meet your p50 target with headroom, and simplifies egress IP stability. Hosted with PrivateLink is lower up-front but may need more engineering work to scale endpoints for bursts and slightly higher per-token costs. we'll send a one-pager with estimates.
[08:13] Priya: compliance — send SOC2, ISO27001, and penetration test summary. we also need details on data retention windows for logs.
[08:24] Jordan: yes we'll send the security pack (link to docs noted), and Samira will attach the KMS integration guide.
[08:32] Samira: quick network nit: if you choose peering, remember route table size and transitive routing; if you have multiple VPCs you might want a transit gateway. PrivateLink avoids transitive routing but brings per-endpoint scaling considerations.
[08:52] Ben: do you support PrivateLink for eu-west-1? any limitations?
[08:58] Samira: yes we support PrivateLink in eu-west-1. limitation is throughput per endpoint and cross-account DNAT behaviour; we'll include recommended throughput targets and how many endpoints to provision per load.
[09:12] Miguel: success criteria recap — p50 < 200ms (on dedicated), sustained 100 rps, 200 burst, all data contained in eu-west-1, metadata audit logs exported to our SIEM, and KMS BYOK — is that accurate?
[09:28] Jordan: yep, that's the working list. we'll add clarity on exact metrics and measurement methodology in the benchmark spec.
[09:36] Priya: one more — attestations for data residency: we need written confirmation that model hosting and logs remain in the region for the POC.
[09:46] Samira: we can provide a scoped attestation for the POC and the config to ensure region pinning. for production contracts we'll have contractual clauses.
[09:56] Miguel: okay good. operational checks — what telemetry do we expose so we can correlate API calls with internal request IDs? we need request-id passthrough.
[10:06] Samira: we support customer-provided request IDs in headers (x-request-id) and surface a mapping in the request logs. we also provide token-level latency breakdowns in the console for per-route analysis.
[10:20] Ben: about the POC environment — will it be single-tenant for the POC or multi-tenant?
[10:26] Samira: for the POC we can provision a dedicated pool (logical dedicated) to mimic production; if you need strict single-tenant hardware we can discuss dedicated hosts but that's higher cost.
[10:38] Miguel: ok. any blockers from your side?
[10:41] Jordan: none immediate — our blockers are: getting CIDR + region confirmation, security review info, and confirmation of the sample dataset approach. once those are in we can schedule the network window.
[10:54] Priya: i'll need the network diagram and the KMS policy draft for review.
[11:00] Samira: i'll attach a network diagram template and sample KMS policy to the follow-up email.
[11:06] Jordan: recap of action items — Jordan send checklist and pricing, Samira send benchmark harness + network diagram + KMS guide, Ben confirm CIDRs/region, Priya run security review. POC target start date proposed: 2026-07-06. does that work?
[11:24] Miguel: tentative yes, pending infra calendar.
[11:28] Ben: i'll confirm by 2026-06-28.
[11:32] Jordan: great. we also agreed to run the bench with 5000 synthetic requests for perf and 1k de-id prompts for quality. Samira you'll share scoring script.
[11:44] Samira: yes will do.
[11:47] Miguel: any mention of fallback behavior if the primary model OOMs?
[11:51] Samira: yes we support automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants and automatic reroute to another capacity pool; we'll test that in the POC failover scenarios.
[12:03] Jordan: ok final notes — we'll send the security pack and POC plan today, expect follow up email with links. thanks everyone.
[12:12] Miguel: thanks, bye.

Links referenced: https://redwood.example/docs/security-pack.pdf (SOC2/ISO), https://redwood.example/network/vpc-peering-checklist, repo: https://github.com/redwood-ai/poc-bench-harness (will be shared by Samira)

End of transcript.
